Summaries of Quantitative Trial Designs and Operating Characteristics

Source: R/f_summary_qtd.R
summaryQuantitative.Rd

The standard summary() method supports quantitative decision rules from getDesignQuantitative() and results from getOperatingCharacteristicsMeans() and getOperatingCharacteristicsRates().

Value

A SummaryFactory object supporting console and Markdown output.

Details

Use summary(rule) for the target value, lower reference value and decision percentiles. Use summary(oc) for the decision rule, assumptions and category probabilities. Each sample-size scenario has a separate table, with one row per alternative and one column per decision category. Categories are retained separately; probabilities are neither recomputed nor aggregated. Rates tables show the treatment event probability and the beneficial risk difference. Their assumptions include the control event probability, beneficial direction and selected interval method.

The digits and output arguments follow summary.ParameterSet(). The output parts are "title", "overview", "body" and "all". For a decision rule, the body contains its parameters. For operating characteristics, the overview contains the rule and assumptions, and the body contains the tables. Summary precision follows rpact.summary.digits and rpact.summary.digits.probs. The summary keeps a copy of the supplied object, so later changes to the original do not change an existing summary.

Print a summary with print(summary(oc), markdown = TRUE) to obtain Markdown with probability tables. Console tables use wrapped, readable column names.

See also

summary.ParameterSet()

Examples

rule <- getDesignQuantitative(targetValue = 0, lowerReferenceValue = -0.05)
rates <- getOperatingCharacteristicsRates(rule,
    numberOfSubjects = matrix(c(75, 75, 75, 150), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE),
    pi1 = c(0.1, 0.15, 0.175, 0.2, 0.25), pi2 = 0.15, directionUpper = FALSE)
summary(rates)
